question: Internet Access restored in Iran by June 30, 2026?
reasoning: The vault's [[entities/iran]] entity documents the regime's pattern of using internet blackouts as a control mechanism during unrest. The new [[threads/iran-internet-restrictions]] thread (created this cycle) captures the pattern: (1) Iran has one of the most sophisticated censorship systems globally, (2) blackouts typically last 5-14 days for protest-related events but war-related blackouts can last much longer, (3) restoration is always partial — social media and international bandwidth remain restricted. The February 28, 2026 blackout is war-related (Iran-US-Israel military engagement) and has already lasted ~80+ days as of May 20. This breaks the historical pattern of 5-14 day blackouts. Full internet restoration before June 30 (~41 days away) would require the regime to decide it no longer needs wartime information control. Given the unresolved state of Iran's post-war situation and regime stability concerns, the structural bias is toward continued restriction. The 21% market price is slightly above the historical baseline for quick restoration and I'd place probability at 15-20%.
